Munificence

/myoo-NIF-uh-suhns/ - the stress falls on NIF · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Munificence means extraordinary generosity in giving.

Whole wings of the aquarium exist only because of one trawler magnate's munificence.

Worked Example

The stonecutters' guild still reads aloud, each founding day, what the quarry's first owner gave it in a single decade: new derricks, a bridge for its wagons, a pension for every widow of the craft, and the seam of white marble it works to this day.

Munificence is the exact word for that decade of giving, because munificence means extraordinary generosity in giving — the scale is the point. Generosity covers a borrowed ladder and a covered lunch; munificence builds bridges and endows pensions, giving at a size that changes what a town can be.

How Munificence Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

lavishness

lavishness: spending on a grand scale, giving or not

bountifulness

bountifulness: plentiful supply — the harvest word for the same plenty

Antonyms

penny-pinching

penny-pinching: counting every coin twice before parting with it

hoarding

hoarding: keeping it all, giving none

How Strong Is It? — kindness → generosity → munificence

kindness vs. munificence

kindness vs. munificence: Kindness can cost nothing at all — a held door or a patient answer already counts.

generosity vs. munificence

generosity vs. munificence: Generosity goes further than kindness — something real is given away — but ordinary generosity is within anyone's reach, while munificence funds bridges and endowments.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of munificence.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — muni

Root — muni: gift, duty (Latin munus)

Root — fic

Root — fic: to make, to do (from Latin facere)

Suffix — -ence

Suffix — -ence: noun ending: the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Muni (gift) + fic (to make) + -ence = the quality of gift-making. Latin munificus described a person whose gifts were their trade — someone who makes gifts the way a smith makes hinges — and the English word keeps that scale: production-line generosity, extraordinary in size.

Use the root in a new word: municipal

Use the root in a new word: municipal: Municipal services — the water main, the streetlights — belong to a town that took its duties into its own hands; Latin munus meant both the gift and the duty.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / grand

Munificence is the formal, marble-lobby word for giving of extraordinary scale. Largess, its unit-mate, shines differently — a shower of lavish gifts, often with an audience; munificence weighs more and shows off less. For everyday givers, generosity is the honest size, and the benefactor is the person behind any of the three.
